watchlist.thesis: Defensive utility relative strength: ED rose 0.82% on Nov 19 and lost only 0.15% over five sessions versus XLU -2.34% and SPY -5.10%, but the Nov 16 six-million-share offering and 0.74× recent average volume leave a supply overhang and require follow-through.

Insurance relative strength held near flat (-0.42%) over five sessions and gained 0.33% on Nov 19 while XLF fell 5.28%, with a strong technical reading; below-average volume still requires a confirmed breakout.

sector_notes: Over Nov 13–19, utilities (XLU -2.34%) and consumer staples (XLP -2.70%) were the relative leaders, outperforming SPY (-5.10%); the only defensible long bias is selective defensive relative strength. Energy (-6.27%), healthcare (-6.03%), technology (-5.63%), communication services (-5.46%) and financials (-5.28%) lagged, while Nov 19 breadth collapsed to 428 advancers versus 2,507 decliners among U.S. stocks priced at least $5 with at least 500,000 shares traded. Selling remained concentrated in high-beta AI, semiconductor and data-center names, so require volume confirmation and avoid chasing isolated rebounds.
